labctl.notes: RETRONET BRIDGE (2026-08-22): n0 is a tap on vmbr-rn (NOT slirp); the guest is a DHCP client on the reserved 10.99.0.16/24 with NO default route (rn-tapnet.sh + the fail-closed guard chain BEOSRN-IN, which aborts the launch if it does not verify). PS/2 RELATIVE pointer (pointerRel) -- R5 has no absolute tablet, and it applies its own acceleration, so scripted pointer work must be closed-loop (slam to 0,0, step, screendump, correct). exec = telnet_unix_e: labctl exec beos over BeOS R5's OWN telnetd at 10.99.0.16:23 over the bridge (no hostfwd, no agent in the guest, no port forward), user baron, password from the station dir's telnet-exec.passwd which the launcher writes from registry/local.env; client /root/sunexec.py with SUN_RC=$? because R5's login shell is bash. R5's ftpd is on :21 the same way for file transfer. KDL/kernel debug still lands on serial.log. See docs/lab/retronet/STATION-beos.md.

render.stationsManifestPrelude:
# beos (VMID 143) - BeOS R5 Professional 5.0.3, the original behind haiku.
#   TCG (R5 #GPs under KVM: unhandled MSRs), pentium3, 1 CPU, 512 MB, IDE
#   qcow2 on an MBR partition, std VGA at the vesa-settings 1024x768x16, PS/2
#   relative pointer via the daemon's abs->rel path. RETRONET: rtl8139 on a tap
#   on vmbr-rn (DHCP-reserved 10.99.0.16, no default route, guard chain
#   BEOSRN-IN); ne2k_pci was the NIC until 2026-08-23 and had to go -- R5's
#   etherpci driver storms 'bad next packet' and dies under a real page load.
#   VERBATIM launcher with conditional -loadvm golden. Two fixes live INSIDE the
#   volume: config_manager/isa removed (PnP BIOS call page-faults input_server
#   under SeaBIOS) and multiprocessor_support disabled (PCI IRQs via the PIC).

museum.blurb: Be Inc.'s BeOS R5 (2000) — the multithreaded media OS behind Haiku's yellow tabs, running as it shipped.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. BeOS R5 Professional 5.0.3 installed from the archive.org Pro CD onto an MBR BFS partition; TCG-only (KVM #GP). Archetype: beige-tower-crt; a BeBox would be the ideal model but R5 x86 shipped on commodity PCs. On the retronet since 2026-08-23: rtl8139 on vmbr-rn, DHCP 10.99.0.16, browsing the museum corpus in NetPositive, and signed in to the museum's own ICQ gateway as UIN 50000 with ICBM .71 (the BeCQ successor, 2001) over the pre-OSCAR UDP-4000 door — the only station on the fleet that uses it; HiveBot greets a visitor about half a minute after the client signs on. See docs/lab/retronet/STATION-beos.md.

launcherParity.reason: tracked verbatim launcher is the deployed launcher. Absolute pointer landed 2026-08-30: a `-chardev socket` plus `-device kh-ramabs` writing app_server's own pointer coordinate. kh-ramabs registers NO VMStateDescription and touches no emulated hardware, so it adds no section to the migration stream and does not change the device set -- PROVEN on a sandbox rig, where `-loadvm` succeeded with the device attached. What DOES force a golden re-bake is the BINARY: the 2026-08-23 golden was baked under the host pve-qemu-kvm package and carries a Proxmox-only `pbs-state` vmstate section, so a standalone build refuses it with `Unknown section or instance 'pbs-state' 0` (measured). Moving beos onto its own /opt/qemu-beos build therefore needs ONE cold re-bake, after which the station stops depending on the shared host package entirely. INSTALL ORDER IS BINDING: binary before launcher (`-device kh-ramabs` is an unknown device on an older binary and QEMU refuses to start), and the launcher is safe to deploy first only because it omits the device when KH_RAMABS_ADDR is unset.

pointerRamAddress.status: PENDING the cold re-bake under /opt/qemu-beos; deliberately null rather than a stale value
pointerRamAddress.note: Guest-physical address of BeOS R5 app_server's own pointer coordinate -- the input the kh-ramabs control object writes, as two little-endian int32. It is valid ONLY for the golden it was derived against: `loadvm golden` restores RAM verbatim, so the address is fixed for the life of THAT checkpoint and no longer, and a re-bake moves it. Two addresses were derived and proven during bring-up (0x038f1ae4 on one cold boot of the pristine volume, a different one on the restored 2026-08-23 golden) which is exactly why none of them is recorded here as production truth. RE-DERIVE IT after every re-bake with the four-sample pmemsave bias search in docs/lab/BEOS-ABSOLUTE-POINTER.md (about twenty minutes, mechanical). Beware the four DERIVED copies that track the pointer perfectly and are not inputs -- only a write test separates them. kh-ramabs verifies the address at connect and refuses every write if verification fails, so a stale address degrades this station to its relative path rather than corrupting guest memory.

qemuBuild.base: QEMU 11.0.2 (the same version as the host pve-qemu-kvm 11.0.2-1, so machine type pc-i440fx-11.0 is unchanged)
qemuBuild.note: 0001 is NOT optional on a standalone build: on the host package the fast-poll patch arrives as pve quilt slot 0047, and a build without it silently drops this tile back to the stock 30 ms display scan. BeOS R5 was booted cold to its full desktop on this build during bring-up, so R5 does not depend on anything the pve patches add. 0009 is macos753's layout-table restructure and 0010 extends it, so the two are ordered and not interchangeable; all four verified to apply in order and to compile under -Werror. binarySha256 is deliberately ABSENT until a binary is actually installed at the prefix -- recording a sha for an artifact nobody deployed would be a confident-looking value that was never measured.
